STATEMENT

Architecture, for me, begins with attention. I draw buildings before I design them — courtyards, stairwells, the gap between two walls where light lands at four in the afternoon. The four projects in this portfolio move between three scales: the dense city, the single structure, and the void that gives both meaning. What I hope you find here is not polish, but a way of thinking — measuring carefully, building slowly, and treating light as a material as real as timber or concrete.

01

Vertical Alleys

HOUSING STUDY · CHIPBOARD MODELS 1:200 · 2025

A study of high-density housing that keeps the street life of the old alley. Twelve units are stacked around one continuous vertical lane, so that neighbours still meet each other on the way home. At 1:200, chipboard models were used to test how daylight reaches the lower courtyards, and how the lane narrows and widens like the alleys it remembers.

STEP 1

Site survey

Three alleys measured by foot; widths, heights and daily light recorded in a pocket notebook.

STEP 2

Massing studies

Twelve units arranged and rearranged around a single vertical lane until every home touched it.

STEP 3

1:200 model

Chipboard volumes; the lane cut open to trace daylight down to the lowest courtyard.

STEP 4

Observation

Afternoon light re-tested across four hours; the lane widened where shade gathered too long.

02

Timber Pavilion

SMALL STRUCTURE · TIMBER BATTENS 1:20 · 2025

A small pavilion for a university garden, framed in reusable timber battens. The structure follows one rule: every joint must be assembled by two people, without metal fasteners. The roof geometry was resolved entirely by hand drawing before the 1:20 model was cut — the pencil lines are still visible under the final frame.

03

Old Town Theatre

ADAPTIVE REUSE · PLASTER MODEL 1:100 · 2024

Adaptive reuse of a 1930s cinema in the old town. The intervention keeps the original facade untouched and inserts a new white shell inside, so that visitors can read the layers of time in section. The building was surveyed by hand, redrawn at 1:100, and tested as a plaster model that separates — old and new lifting apart.

FIG.03C — THE WHITE SHELL LIFTED FROM THE OLD WALLS1:100

04

Courtyard of Light

FIELD STUDY · PHOTOGRAPHY · 2023

Light is the only material in this study. One courtyard, four visits, four hours of the day. These photographs record how a single space changes its mind between morning and evening — and they are the reason I chose architecture in the first place.
